v4.9.087 - everything carries a time, so nothing wins by not having one (#378, #379)

#379 THE LAST PLACE WORK COULD DISAPPEAR SILENTLY.

     Found by the random day, which reported three of the tablet's sentences
     missing on the desktop and was right.

     What happened: after a pull, a device forgets which frames the server
     already has, so its next push sends EVERY frame — the log says "5/5 frames
     changed" — including ones it never touched. An untouched frame carries no
     change time, because nothing changed on it. And a frame with no time cannot
     lose a comparison: when the server's own copy also had no time, the rule
     fell back to whichever row arrived most recently. So the device that
     reconnected LAST overwrote the other's work, without a word.

     That is the shape behind every "the later change went missing" report.

     Roman's fix, and better than the two I proposed: everything carries a time.
     A frame this device has not changed now says ZERO — the oldest time there
     is — instead of saying nothing. It loses to any real edit, everywhere,
     always. No new column, nothing asked of the other device, two lines at the
     sending end.

     The rule that judges this was already correct and has been since #311: a
     copy that knows when it changed beats one that does not. It simply never
     got the chance, because both sides were silent.

#378 DELETING A FRAME IS FINAL — decided, not fixed.

     The same random day kept reporting a lost sentence: a frame deleted on one
     device while offline, written on by the other a moment later. The deletion
     won and took the writing with it.

     Two reasons to leave it that way. The server does not hide a deleted frame,
     it destroys it — row, versions, drawings, pictures — so there is nothing to
     bring back. And this is one person's app: whoever deleted the frame is the
     same person who wrote on it from the other device a second earlier. Roman:
     "someone deleting a frame should be aware of doing it."

     Two tests now hold that rule in both directions, so it stays a decision
     rather than drifting into an accident. And the ledger no longer calls a
     deliberate deletion "lost work" — once deleted, it stays deleted.

     Hidden is untouched and stays as it is: a hidden frame keeps everything and
     comes back only through Un-Hide.

32 of 32 pass, including the day that lost the three sentences, replayed with
the same seed.
